quality_notes: Curious Refuge Labs scored it 8.26/10 overall (review headline states 8.29/10). Category scores: Prompt Adherence 8.11/10, Temporal Consistency 8.0/10, Visual Fidelity 8.44/10, Motion Quality 8.0/10, Style & Cinematic Realism 7.77/10. Described as a "physics-first" model with a clear priority hierarchy — when compute is exhausted it sacrifices Prompt Adherence to preserve Temporal Consistency, Motion Quality, then Visual Fidelity. Peak results (perfect 10/10 scores) require "geometric tethering": a large, high-contrast anchor element fixed in frame plus contact friction, floor anchoring, deep Z-axis with shallow depth of field, and one clean camera vector (e.g. "slow push-in"). Spatial prepositions (against, around, in front of) and cinematic grammar drive realism. Weakness: 2D animation collapses Temporal Consistency (3.0–6.0 range) because flat planes lack high-detail anchors and stable tracking markers, causing drift; the model is forced to re-resolve the subject every frame. Pretrained motion maps trigger automatically on human movement with no interpretation, and prompts with competing motion vectors degrade motion quality.
notes: Specs: max duration 15s native (moves beyond the 5-10s loop phase into full narrative arcs); max resolution up to 4K native (no upscaling artifacts, ready for high-end commercial use); frame rate 30-60fps (60fps enables hyper-smooth motion and professional slow-motion); native audio sync (generates sound effects and speech simultaneously with video); motion control via puppeteering tools with high-difficulty physics handling (fighting, hugging, object interaction). Review is stated as non-biased and not affiliated with Kling. Competitive positioning: stronger than Veo 3.1, which is described as "not as stable or reliable as Kling 3.0"; weaker than Sora 2 on character consistency and prompt logic; behind Runway on style-transfer and experimental creative tools. Recommended for AI video artists due to high fidelity ceiling, mathematical predictability, and cinematic control. Author: Brian Dalton, Curious Refuge, published Feb 26.
